title: Bitcoin and ether edge higher; payments expansion and exchange restrictions shape the news
paragraphs: Bitcoin traded near $85,310, up 0.8% over 24 hours, while ether gained 0.6% to about $2,700. The wider market picture was mixed. CoinGecko reported total crypto market capitalization of $2.89 trillion, down 2.8%, even as the two largest assets rose. Bitcoin accounted for roughly 59% of that total. The gains in BTC and ETH therefore do not establish a broad market recovery.

The latest US jobs report provides a subdued economic backdrop: payrolls increased by 29,000 and unemployment was 4.2%. The Bureau of Labor Statistics described both measures as little changed. Modest hiring can reduce pressure for tighter monetary policy, but it also raises questions about demand. For crypto, those are competing influences on risk appetite. The report alone does not establish why prices moved or what the Federal Reserve will do next.

OpenPayd is targeting a Nasdaq listing by year-end and a US service launch by April 2027, CEO Iana Dimitrova told CoinDesk. Its proposed merger with Titan Acquisition Corp. still needs the registration statement to become effective and shareholder approval. The company combines conventional payments infrastructure with stablecoin services and has brought 43 state money-transmitter licenses into its group. A listing could finance expansion and acquisitions, increasing the infrastructure available to businesses moving between bank money and stablecoins. These remain plans with approvals and execution ahead.

In Iran, the central bank plans to block rial bank accounts and payment gateways at some crypto exchanges over concerns about manipulation in Tether trading, according to Crypto Briefing. Losing those connections would make local-currency deposits and withdrawals harder. Earlier restrictions limited USDT purchases and trading hours. The new report describes planned banking restrictions, with the affected exchanges and implementation still uncertain. The practical risk is reduced access to the exchange funding channels people use to obtain stablecoins.

Our portfolio stands at about $130,368: $13,371 in the active treasury and $116,997 in the cold-storage Safe. Its displayed value is $11,282 lower, or 8.0%, than the previous comparable snapshot. The Safe still holds 26.74 million ARC directly, now worth $97,776. That unchanged balance lost $10,534 in valuation, accounting for most of the portfolio decline. Direct ARC represents 75% of the total, and the two WETH/ARC pools hold another $16,423 combined.

The treasury also holds $4,870 of cbETH, $1,944 across Beefy USDC/cbMEGA positions and $555 on Hyperliquid. Across both wallets, Aave has $9,213 of WETH collateral against $2,925 of USDC debt, with health factors of 3.34 and 2.23. Fluid is only $153 net, but its $1,056 debt and 1.03 health factor leave little liquidation headroom.
